newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia probes claims of BP rights violations.
newsitem.headline: Colombia probes claims of BP rights violations.

text.p: Colombia's top law enforcer has opened an investigation into media allegations that British Petroleum Plc Ltd funded paramilitary groups in the east of the country, the authorities said on Friday.

Chief Prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso launched the preliminary inquiry at the request of John Doust, head of BP's local subsidiary BP Exploration, in a effort to clarify the accusations described by BP as "injurious and offensive."

Claims that BP, Colombia's single-largest foreign investor, paid right-wing death squads to kill local residents opposed to its operations, first surfaced in the British press last year and were based on the findings of a 1995 multi-agency report into human rights violations in Casanare and Arauca provinces.
Valdivieso stressed, however, that the report never contained specific accusations against BP or any other oil company operating in the oil-rich eastern plains region.
"I have given precise instructions for the corresponding investigation to be assigned to the National Human Rights Unit," Valdivieso wrote to Doust, in a letter released by BP on Friday.
"I should point out that the recommendations formulated in the final report of the (multi-agency) commission (in 1995) did not include any suggestions to investigate members of BP," he said.

BP welcomed the move to open the preliminary inquiry saying: "BP Exploration reaffirms its activities are undertaken within the framework of the law ... and is confident this investigation will bring complete clarity to the facts."

The original report, entitled Interinstitutional Commission Report on the Human Rights Situation in Casanare and Arauca, documented the killings of scores of peasant activists, allegedly carried out by paramilitary groups or the army.
BP was not specifically named or directly linked to any of those incidents.

The report did, however, blame the oil industry for the social destabilization of the region, saying it had created false hopes of work and fueled prostitution, drug-dealing and crime among those unable to find employment in the sector.
